Study guide · efficient attention

Linear Attention

Trading an unbounded cache for a fixed-size state — what that buys, what it costs, and why the chunk size is the whole story.

Mathematical derivations and worked exercises

Each derivation states its assumptions, shows the intermediate steps, and explains what follows. Try each exercise before opening its worked solution.

  1. Derivation: derive the causal kernel recurrence with all dimensions visible
  2. Derivation: locate the state-memory crossover with precision and head sharing
  3. Derivation: derive a gated chunk update rather than hiding decay inside one symbol
  4. Derivation: derive memory half-life and numerical gate accumulation
  5. Derivation: derive exact overwrite, interference, and the stable learning-rate interval
  6. Derivation: turn sequential delta updates into a triangular chunk solve
  7. Derivation: unroll an SSM and see the attention-shaped matrix
  8. Derivation: prove a finite-state recall lower bound by counting

§How to use this document

Companion to the Sparse Attention and LLM Inference Systems guides. Sparse attention bounds the read set; linear attention bounds the state. They attack the same cost from opposite directions and the trade-offs are completely different.

  • Pass 1. §0–§1. The associativity trick, the RNN duality, and the three computation forms. §1 is the part that matters most for hardware and the part most treatments skip.
  • Pass 2. §2–§6. Why the naive version fails and the two families of fix (gating, delta rule), then the theory that explains the ceiling.
  • Pass 3. §7–§9. What actually ships (spoiler: hybrids, at ratios between 3:1 and 7:1), the hardware chapter, and a decision table.

Assumed background: softmax attention, KV caching, and comfort with matrix algebra. No state-space-model background needed — §5 derives the connection rather than assuming it.

If a term is unfamiliar, it is defined. Appendix B explains the linear algebra (outer products, Householder reflections, the WY representation, semiseparable matrices), the learning-theory framing (delta rule, online SGD, Ω lower bounds) and the hardware vocabulary from scratch. Appendix C is a one-line glossary.

The thesis, up front

Linear attention replaces a context-growing KV representation with a fixed-dimensional recurrent state. At fixed width this gives constant memory in context length and constant per-token update cost, while finite precision imposes a worst-case information limit. Smarter write rules improve how the state allocates that capacity; hybrid models supplement it with a smaller number of full-attention layers. Neither learned KV retrieval nor a learned recurrent state is automatically a lossless encoding of the input.

0The trade

Problems defining this stage. Early linear attention replaces a growing token-addressable cache with fixed-dimensional sufficient statistics of a factorized kernel. The core question is which information that state can preserve, not just whether associative multiplication removes quadratic computation.

0.1 What the KV cache really is

Full attention retains the computed key and value vectors for every available context position, creating a growing content-addressable representation. Retaining them avoids the fixed-state compression used by linear attention, but does not make the representation lossless with respect to raw text or guarantee perfect learned retrieval. The cost grows with the stored context.

MKV=2nHkvdhLp(linear in n)Bdecode/token=O(n)(read the whole cache)Fprefill=O(n2d)\begin{aligned}M_{\mathrm{KV}}&=2nH_{\mathrm{kv}}d_hLp\quad\text{(linear in }n\text{)}\\ B_{\mathrm{decode/token}}&=O(n)\quad\text{(read the whole cache)}\\ F_{\mathrm{prefill}}&=O(n^2d)\end{aligned}MKV​Bdecode/token​Fprefill​​=2nHkv​dh​Lp(linear in n)=O(n)(read the whole cache)=O(n2d)​

Linear attention asks: what if instead of storing nnn key–value pairs, we store a single d×dd\times dd×d matrix that summarises them?

Mstate=dkdvHLp(independent of n)Bdecode/token=O(1)(read the state)Fprefill=O(nd2)\begin{aligned}M_{\mathrm{state}}&=d_kd_vHLp\quad\text{(independent of }n\text{)}\\ B_{\mathrm{decode/token}}&=O(1)\quad\text{(read the state)}\\ F_{\mathrm{prefill}}&=O(nd^2)\end{aligned}Mstate​Bdecode/token​Fprefill​​=dk​dv​HLp(independent of n)=O(1)(read the state)=O(nd2)​

The trade is a context-growing collection of KV vectors versus a fixed number of recurrent scalars. With bounded precision, a fixed state cannot retain an unbounded number of independent facts with zero error. The exact capacity limit depends on the fact distribution, feature width, value width, precision, and required error; n>dn>dn>d alone is not a universal threshold at which every useful fact disappears.

0.2 The associativity trick

Write attention without the softmax, using a general similarity kernel sim⁡(q,k)\operatorname{sim}(q, k)sim(q,k):

oi=∑j≤isim⁡(qi,kj)vj∑j≤isim⁡(qi,kj)sim⁡softmax(q,k)=exp⁡ ⁣(q⊤kd)No fixed finite exact feature map for arbitrary inputs.sim⁡linear(q,k)=ϕ(q)⊤ϕ(k)(factorizable)\begin{aligned}o_i&=\frac{\sum_{j\le i}\operatorname{sim}(q_i,k_j)v_j}{\sum_{j\le i}\operatorname{sim}(q_i,k_j)}\\ \operatorname{sim}_{\mathrm{softmax}}(q,k)&=\exp\!\left(\frac{q^\top k}{\sqrt d}\right)\\ &\text{No fixed finite exact feature map for arbitrary inputs.}\\ \operatorname{sim}_{\mathrm{linear}}(q,k)&=\phi(q)^\top\phi(k)\quad\text{(factorizable)}\end{aligned}oi​simsoftmax​(q,k)simlinear​(q,k)​=∑j≤i​sim(qi​,kj​)∑j≤i​sim(qi​,kj​)vj​​=exp(d​q⊤k​)No fixed finite exact feature map for arbitrary inputs.=ϕ(q)⊤ϕ(k)(factorizable)​

If the similarity factorises, the sums reassociate — and that single algebraic move is the whole subject:

oi=∑j(ϕ(qi)⊤ϕ(kj))vj⊤∑jϕ(qi)⊤ϕ(kj)(linear scan)=ϕ(qi)⊤(∑jϕ(kj)vj⊤)ϕ(qi)⊤(∑jϕ(kj))Prefix summaries: O(1) in context length per query.\begin{aligned}o_i&=\frac{\sum_j(\phi(q_i)^\top\phi(k_j))v_j^\top}{\sum_j\phi(q_i)^\top\phi(k_j)}\quad\text{(linear scan)}\\ &=\frac{\phi(q_i)^\top\left(\sum_j\phi(k_j)v_j^\top\right)}{\phi(q_i)^\top\left(\sum_j\phi(k_j)\right)}\\ &\text{Prefix summaries: }O(1)\text{ in context length per query.}\end{aligned}oi​​=∑j​ϕ(qi​)⊤ϕ(kj​)∑j​(ϕ(qi​)⊤ϕ(kj​))vj⊤​​(linear scan)=ϕ(qi​)⊤(∑j​ϕ(kj​))ϕ(qi​)⊤(∑j​ϕ(kj​)vj⊤​)​Prefix summaries: O(1) in context length per query.​

The summaries Si=∑j≤iϕ(kj)vj⊤S_i=\sum_{j\le i}\phi(k_j)v_j^\topSi​=∑j≤i​ϕ(kj​)vj⊤​ and zi=∑j≤iϕ(kj)z_i=\sum_{j\le i}\phi(k_j)zi​=∑j≤i​ϕ(kj​) depend on the causal prefix endpoint i. At a fixed prefix they do not depend on the query vector, so update them once per new token and read them with a matrix–vector product. Katharopoulos et al. use ϕ(x)=elu⁡(x)+1\phi(x)=\operatorname{elu}(x)+1ϕ(x)=elu(x)+1; strict positivity is sufficient for a positive denominator on a nonempty prefix in exact arithmetic, although numerical underflow still needs care.

Derivation: derive the causal kernel recurrence with all dimensions visible

Notation. Queries and keys lie in ℝd; values lie in ℝd_v; the feature map φ sends ℝd to ℝm. Assume φ(q)⊤φ(k) is nonnegative and the prefix denominator is positive. The recurrence is exact for this chosen kernel, not generally for softmax attention.

  1. At position i, expand the numerator as Σj≤i(φ(qi)⊤φ(kj))vj⊤.
  2. Factor φ(qi)⊤ out of the sum because it is the same for every j. The remaining outer products have shape m×dv.
  3. Perform the same distributive operation in the denominator. The two summaries depend on the prefix endpoint i, but not on the particular query once that prefix is fixed.
Si=∑j≤iϕ(kj)vj⊤∈Rm×dvzi=∑j≤iϕ(kj)∈RmSi=Si−1+ϕ(ki)vi⊤,zi=zi−1+ϕ(ki)oi⊤=ϕ(qi)⊤Siϕ(qi)⊤zi\begin{aligned}S_i&=\sum_{j\le i}\phi(k_j)v_j^\top\in\mathbb R^{m\times d_v}\\ z_i&=\sum_{j\le i}\phi(k_j)\in\mathbb R^m\\ S_i&=S_{i-1}+\phi(k_i)v_i^\top,\quad z_i=z_{i-1}+\phi(k_i)\\ o_i^\top&=\frac{\phi(q_i)^\top S_i}{\phi(q_i)^\top z_i}\end{aligned}Si​zi​Si​oi⊤​​=j≤i∑​ϕ(kj​)vj⊤​∈Rm×dv​=j≤i∑​ϕ(kj​)∈Rm=Si−1​+ϕ(ki​)vi⊤​,zi​=zi−1​+ϕ(ki​)=ϕ(qi​)⊤zi​ϕ(qi​)⊤Si​​​

Each update/read costs O(mdv) and stores mdv+m scalars, independent of prefix length. A strictly positive feature map is sufficient to make a nonempty prefix denominator positive in exact arithmetic. Nonnegativity alone permits a zero denominator, and adding ε changes the operator slightly. Causality means there is a different Si at each prefix; using Sn for every training position would leak future tokens.

Why not factor softmax exactly? The exponential dot-product kernel has the series exp(qᵀk)=Σr≥0(qᵀk)r/r!, corresponding to infinitely many polynomial features. It admits feature representations and finite approximations, but no fixed finite feature dimension exactly represents it for arbitrary inputs. A finite feature map imposes a rank bound m on every unmasked Gram matrix; exponential-kernel Gram matrices can have arbitrarily high rank. Random features or truncated expansions buy approximations with their own error and cost. Reassociation is exact algebra once a finite kernel is chosen; choosing that kernel is the modeling change.

Exercise — Verify the recurrence by direct attention

Use φ as the identity on nonnegative vectors. Let k₁=(1,0), v₁=2, k₂=(1,1), v₂=4, and q₂=(1,2). Compute S₂,z₂ and the normalized output. Check it by evaluating both kernel scores directly.

Show worked solution

With scalar values, S is a two-entry column. S₂=(1,0)ᵀ·2+(1,1)ᵀ·4=(6,4)ᵀ, and z₂=(2,1)ᵀ. The numerator is (1,2)·(6,4)=14 and denominator (1,2)·(2,1)=4, giving o₂=3.5. Direct scores are q₂ᵀk₁=1 and q₂ᵀk₂=3; their normalized weighted value is (1·2+3·4)/(1+3)=3.5. The equality is algebraic, with no approximation for this kernel.

0.3 Therefore: attention is an RNN

Because the sums are prefix sums, they have a recurrence:

St=St−1+ϕ(kt)vt⊤,S∈Rd×dzt=zt−1+ϕ(kt)ot=ϕ(qt)⊤Stϕ(qt)⊤zt\begin{aligned}S_t&=S_{t-1}+\phi(k_t)v_t^\top,\quad S\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\\ z_t&=z_{t-1}+\phi(k_t)\\ o_t&=\frac{\phi(q_t)^\top S_t}{\phi(q_t)^\top z_t}\end{aligned}St​zt​ot​​=St−1​+ϕ(kt​)vt⊤​,S∈Rd×d=zt−1​+ϕ(kt​)=ϕ(qt​)⊤zt​ϕ(qt​)⊤St​​​
The duality that organises everything

A linear-attention layer is a linear RNN whose hidden state is a matrix, and the write operation is an outer product kv⊤k v^\top kv⊤. This is classical associative memory — a Hopfield-style "write the key–value binding into a matrix, read it back by multiplying with the key." Every architecture in this guide is a different answer to: how should the state be updated when a new (k,v) arrives?

Reading the same equations in the other direction: at decode time you keep one d×dd\times dd×d matrix per head instead of a growing cache. Memory per token is O(1)O(1)O(1), the arithmetic per token is O(d2)O(d^{2})O(d2) instead of O(n⋅d)O(n\cdot d)O(n⋅d), and the cost is independent of position in the sequence. For a serving system this is a completely different cost model — see §8.1.

Derivation: locate the state-memory crossover with precision and head sharing

Compare equal layer counts, one sequence. A softmax layer stores n keys and n values per KV head, each of width d and bkv bytes. A linear layer stores Hr independent m×dv recurrent matrices with bs bytes per state scalar. Include a normalizer of m scalars per head when the method uses one. Projection parameters are separate and cancel only if the architectures really match.

MKV(n)=2nHkvdbkvMstate={Hr(mdv+m)bs,normalized kernelHrmdvbs,unnormalized recurrencenmemory-cross=Mstate2Hkvdbkv\begin{aligned}M_{\mathrm{KV}}(n)&=2nH_{\mathrm{kv}}db_{\mathrm{kv}}\\ M_{\mathrm{state}}&=\begin{cases}H_r(md_v+m)b_s,&\text{normalized kernel}\\ H_rmd_vb_s,&\text{unnormalized recurrence}\end{cases}\\ n_{\mathrm{memory\text{-}cross}}&=\frac{M_{\mathrm{state}}}{2H_{\mathrm{kv}}db_{\mathrm{kv}}}\end{aligned}MKV​(n)Mstate​nmemory-cross​​=2nHkv​dbkv​={Hr​(mdv​+m)bs​,Hr​mdv​bs​,​normalized kernelunnormalized recurrence​=2Hkv​dbkv​Mstate​​​

Take Hr=32, Hkv=8, m=dv=d=128, FP32 state and BF16 KV. Ignoring the small normalizer, Mstate=32·128²·4=2,097,152 bytes per layer, while each context token adds 2·8·128·2=4,096 KV bytes. The storage crossover is n=512. At n=131,072 and 64 layers, KV occupies 32 GiB and the FP32 state occupies 128 MiB, a 256× ratio. BF16 state would halve its capacity but changes numerical behavior.

This is a storage crossover, not the empirical runtime crossover near a few thousand tokens in specific papers. Runtime includes state reads and writes, GQA reuse, short convolutions, chunk kernels, and hardware occupancy. Treat state capacity, state traffic, and arithmetic as separate ledgers. A constant-size state remains constant in n even if it resides in HBM; spilling it does not restore a context-growing cache, though it can make the constant expensive.

1Three computation forms — the part that matters for hardware

Problems defining this stage. A recurrence with attractive asymptotic cost can still underuse accelerator matrix units. This stage asks how to express the same sequence operator as recurrent, parallel and chunkwise computations so training throughput and decode-state size can be optimized together.

The same layer can be computed three ways with identical results and wildly different hardware behaviour. If you take one thing from this guide, take this section.

1.1 Parallel, recurrent, chunkwise

FormComplexityParallelismWhen to use
ParallelO(n2d)O(n^{2}d)O(n2d)Full, across the sequenceShort sequences during training. It is a matmul, so it saturates tensor cores — often faster than the "efficient" form below n≈2Kn \approx 2Kn≈2K.
RecurrentO(nd2)O(n d^{2})O(nd2)None across timeDecode. One token at a time is the actual workload, so serialism costs nothing.
ChunkwiseO(nCd+nd2)O(n C d + n d^{2})O(nCd+nd2)Across chunks of size CCCEverything else. Training and prefill at long context.

1.2 Why chunkwise is the answer

Split the sequence into chunks of size CCC. Within a chunk, compute the quadratic form directly (a matmul). Across chunks, pass the state. Each chunk's output is the sum of two terms:

Ointra=(Q[i]K[i]⊤⊙M)V[i](causal mask M)Ointer=Q[i]S[i](prior chunks)O[i]=Ointra+OinterS[i+1]=S[i]+K[i]⊤V[i](ungated update)\begin{aligned}O_{\mathrm{intra}}&=(Q[i]K[i]^\top\odot M)V[i]\quad\text{(causal mask }M\text{)}\\ O_{\mathrm{inter}}&=Q[i]S[i]\quad\text{(prior chunks)}\\ O[i]&=O_{\mathrm{intra}}+O_{\mathrm{inter}}\\ S[i+1]&=S[i]+K[i]^\top V[i]\quad\text{(ungated update)}\end{aligned}Ointra​Ointer​O[i]S[i+1]​=(Q[i]K[i]⊤⊙M)V[i](causal mask M)=Q[i]S[i](prior chunks)=Ointra​+Ointer​=S[i]+K[i]⊤V[i](ungated update)​
Why this is the right shape for silicon
  • Everything is a matmul. No element-wise scan, no sequential dependency inside the chunk. All four operations above hit tensor cores.
  • CCC is a tuning knob between two bad extremes. Small CCC → the serial inter-chunk recurrence dominates and you lose parallelism. Large CCC → the C×CC\times CC×C intra-chunk term reintroduces quadratic cost. Typical sweet spot is CCC = 64–256, chosen so the C×CC\times CC×C tile fits in SRAM.
  • Memory traffic is controllable. Load Q[i],K[i],V[i]Q[i], K[i], V[i]Q[i],K[i],V[i] once, keep SSS on-chip across the whole chunk, write O[i]O[i]O[i] once.
  • It subsumes the other two forms. C=nC = nC=n gives the parallel form; C=1C = 1C=1 gives the recurrent form. There is no separate algorithm to implement.

Derivation: derive a gated chunk update rather than hiding decay inside one symbol

Scalar gates. Work with unnormalized outputs for clarity: St=atSt−1+ktvt⊤, ot⊤=qt⊤St, with at>0 and S0 the state entering a C-token chunk. Define gi=∏u=1..iau and g0=1.

  1. Substitute the recurrence twice: S₂=a₂a₁S₀+a₂k₁v₁ᵀ+k₂v₂ᵀ. Older writes experience more decay.
  2. Induct on i to obtain a product of gates after each write. The write at j is multiplied by aj+1…ai=gi/gj.
  3. Read the state with qi. Separate contributions from the incoming state and from writes inside the chunk.
Si=giS0+∑j≤igigjkjvj⊤oi⊤=giqi⊤S0+∑j≤igigj(qi⊤kj)vj⊤Ointer=diag⁡(g)QS0Ointra=[QK⊤⊙D]V,Dij=1j≤igigjSC=gCS0+K⊤diag⁡ ⁣(gCg1,…,gCgC)V\begin{aligned}S_i&=g_iS_0+\sum_{j\le i}\frac{g_i}{g_j}k_jv_j^\top\\ o_i^\top&=g_iq_i^\top S_0+\sum_{j\le i}\frac{g_i}{g_j}(q_i^\top k_j)v_j^\top\\ O_{\mathrm{inter}}&=\operatorname{diag}(g)QS_0\\ O_{\mathrm{intra}}&=[QK^\top\odot D]V,\quad D_{ij}=\mathbf1_{j\le i}\frac{g_i}{g_j}\\ S_C&=g_CS_0+K^\top\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{g_C}{g_1},\ldots,\frac{g_C}{g_C}\right)V\end{aligned}Si​oi⊤​Ointer​Ointra​SC​​=gi​S0​+j≤i∑​gj​gi​​kj​vj⊤​=gi​qi⊤​S0​+j≤i∑​gj​gi​​(qi⊤​kj​)vj⊤​=diag(g)QS0​=[QK⊤⊙D]V,Dij​=1j≤i​gj​gi​​=gC​S0​+K⊤diag(g1​gC​​,…,gC​gC​​)V​

Rows of Q and K are query/key vectors; rows of V are values. Setting every a=1 recovers the simple ungated chunk equations. For fixed a=γ, Dij=γi−j. An update written as “decay·S+KᵀV” is only complete when the write decay factors are already absorbed into K or V. A normalized variant must update its z summary using the same decay law.

One can view each chunk as an affine map S↦AS+B. Two chunks compose as (A₂,B₂)∘(A₁,B₁)=(A₂A₁,A₂B₁+B₂), an associative operation. This explains parallel scan across chunks. It does not promise cheap execution for arbitrary dense A: efficient GLA/SSD forms rely on diagonal, scalar, or otherwise structured transitions.

Exercise — Check the missing write-decay factor

Use scalar state S₀=2, gates a₁=1/2,a₂=1/4, and writes k₁v₁=3,k₂v₂=5. Compute S₂ recurrently and with the chunk formula. What does the incorrect formula (a₁a₂)S₀+3+5 produce?

Show worked solution

Recurrence gives S₁=(1/2)·2+3=4 and S₂=(1/4)·4+5=6. The chunk formula gives (1/8)·2+(1/4)·3+5=0.25+0.75+5=6. The incorrect formula gives 8.25 because the first write should decay by a₂ before reaching the end of the chunk. The newest write has no later gate and therefore no decay factor.

1.3 FlashLinearAttention: the IO-aware version

Core idea. Organize recurrent attention into chunks whose within-chunk interactions and state updates use efficient matrix multiplication. Tiling and state management make the algebraic linear-time formulation useful on real accelerator memory hierarchies.

The design tension is exactly the one you would expect from a hardware perspective: parallelism versus memory traffic. The non-materialization version is optimal when batch × heads already fills the machine; the materialization version is necessary for long-sequence, small-batch training where the SMs would otherwise idle. This is the same choice FlashAttention makes between recomputation and storage, in a different place.

The crossover point, and why it matters commercially

Linear attention is slower than FlashAttention below roughly 2K tokens. Mamba-2 reports the same crossover for its SSD algorithm, becoming ~6× faster than FlashAttention-2 at 16K. Below the crossover you are paying d2d^{2}d2 per token to avoid an n⋅dn\cdot dn⋅d you never incurred. This is why linear attention arrived commercially exactly when 128K-plus contexts became normal, and not before.

2Why naive linear attention doesn't work

The 2020 version is elegant and underperforms badly. Four distinct reasons, each of which spawned a fix.

  1. It never forgets. St=St−1+ϕ(kt)vt⊤S_{t} = S_{t-1} + \phi (k_{t})v_{t}^\top St​=St−1​+ϕ(kt​)vt⊤​ is a pure accumulator. Every token ever written stays written, at full weight, forever. After a few thousand tokens the state is an undifferentiated sum and reading it returns an average of everything — attention dilution. The fix is decay (§3).
  2. Writes interfere. Outer-product writes are not orthogonal. Writing (k2,v2)(k_{2},v_{2})(k2​,v2​) when k2k_{2}k2​ is similar to an existing k1k_{1}k1​ corrupts the value stored for k1k_{1}k1​; there is no mechanism to overwrite a binding. The fix is the delta rule (§4).
  3. The normaliser is unstable. Dividing by ϕ(q)⊤z\phi (q)^\top zϕ(q)⊤z is fragile — zzz grows without bound and the denominator can get very small. In practice everyone replaced it: RetNet uses GroupNorm on the output and exploits its scale invariance; most modern designs drop the explicit denominator entirely and normalise the output instead.
  4. The capacity is genuinely smaller. d×dd\times dd×d numbers cannot hold what n×dn\times dn×d numbers hold. This one is not a bug and cannot be fixed — only priced (§6).

3Fix 1 — decay and gating

Problems defining this stage. Plain accumulation mixes old and new associations indefinitely. Decay and input-dependent gates make retention selective, but useful gating must also permit numerically stable, efficient chunkwise execution.

Give the state a way to forget. The progression is a steady move from "forgetting is a constant" to "forgetting is a learned function of the input, per channel."

Plain:St=St−1+ktvt⊤Fixed decay:St=γSt−1+ktvt⊤(RetNet)Data dependent:St=αtSt−1+ktvt⊤,αt=f(xt)Scalar gate: Mamba-2, HGRN.Channel wise:St=Gt⊙St−1+ktvt⊤Gt∈(0,1)d×d(GLA, KDA)\begin{aligned}\text{Plain:}\quad S_t&=S_{t-1}+k_tv_t^\top\\ \text{Fixed decay:}\quad S_t&=\gamma S_{t-1}+k_tv_t^\top\quad\text{(RetNet)}\\ \text{Data dependent:}\quad S_t&=\alpha_tS_{t-1}+k_tv_t^\top,\quad\alpha_t=f(x_t)\\ &\text{Scalar gate: Mamba-2, HGRN.}\\ \text{Channel wise:}\quad S_t&=G_t\odot S_{t-1}+k_tv_t^\top\\ G_t&\in(0,1)^{d\times d}\quad\text{(GLA, KDA)}\end{aligned}Plain:St​Fixed decay:St​Data dependent:St​Channel wise:St​Gt​​=St−1​+kt​vt⊤​=γSt−1​+kt​vt⊤​(RetNet)=αt​St−1​+kt​vt⊤​,αt​=f(xt​)Scalar gate: Mamba-2, HGRN.=Gt​⊙St−1​+kt​vt⊤​∈(0,1)d×d(GLA, KDA)​
ModelGateWhy it matters
RetNet

Core idea. Apply fixed per-head decay to recurrent memory, using multiple time scales while retaining compatible parallel, recurrent and chunkwise forms.

(2023)		Fixed scalar γ\gamma γ per head, multi-scale across headsDecay as an ALiBi-like positional prior. Because γ\gamma γ is constant, the decay mask is a fixed matrix and all three computation forms stay clean. 7B at 8K: 8.4× faster decode and 70% less memory than a KV-cached transformer, with approximately flat decode latency over the batch range measured in that experiment; this is not a guarantee for arbitrary batch size.
GLA

Core idea. Learn content-dependent channel-wise forgetting and use secondary chunking to isolate numerically delicate gate operations from tensor-core-friendly matrix products.

(2024)		Data-dependent 2-D gate GtG_{t}Gt​, low-rank parameterisedDifferent channels forget at different rates, chosen by the content. The contribution is showing this still admits an efficient chunkwise form — expressiveness that doesn't cost you the hardware story.
Mamba / Mamba-2

Core idea. Make state transitions and input/output mappings depend on the input; Mamba-2 restricts the transition structure so SSD can execute much of the recurrence through matrix multiplication.

Input-dependent Δ,B,C\Delta , B, CΔ,B,C (selectivity)Arrives at the same place from the SSM side (§5). Mamba-2's decay is scalar-times-identity, which is what makes SSD expressible as matmuls.
Lightning Attention

Core idea. Pair a fixed-decay linear recurrence with optimized kernels, emphasizing scalable execution of long-context models.

Fixed decay, heavily optimised kernelsThe variant that scaled first: MiniMax-01 shipped it in a 456B-parameter model with 1M-token context.
RWKV

Core idea. Evolve recurrent time-mixing and channel-wise retention rules while keeping a fixed-size state for token-by-token inference.

(4→7)		Time-decay vectors, evolving toward channel-wise and delta-like rulesThe independently-developed lineage; RWKV-7 converges on much the same design as gated delta rules.
Why gating is not free — the log-space problem

A channel-wise gate means the chunkwise form needs cumulative products of gates. Computed naively these underflow, so you work in log space — but log-space arithmetic cannot use half-precision tensor cores. GLA's answer is secondary-level chunking: split each chunk into sub-chunks, compute inter-sub-chunk interactions with half-precision matmuls and only the intra-sub-chunk part in full precision. This is a pure hardware-driven design decision and a good example of what "hardware-efficient" means in practice.

Derivation: derive memory half-life and numerical gate accumulation

Fixed scalar decay. For St=γSt−1+ktvt⊤, with 0<γ<1, a write j contributes γt−j at t. Setting that multiplier to 1/2 and taking logarithms gives the half-life h=log(1/2)/log γ. The total weight of a constant stream is Σr≥0γr=1/(1−γ). These are different notions of effective horizon.

γ=0.99:t1/2≈68.97,∑j≥0γj=100γ=0.999:t1/2≈692.80,∑j≥0γj=1000wj→t=exp⁡ ⁣(∑u=j+1tlog⁡au)\begin{aligned}\gamma=0.99:&\quad t_{1/2}\approx68.97,\quad\sum_{j\ge0}\gamma^j=100\\ \gamma=0.999:&\quad t_{1/2}\approx692.80,\quad\sum_{j\ge0}\gamma^j=1000\\ w_{j\to t}&=\exp\!\left(\sum_{u=j+1}^t\log a_u\right)\end{aligned}γ=0.99:γ=0.999:wj→t​​t1/2​≈68.97,j≥0∑​γj=100t1/2​≈692.80,j≥0∑​γj=1000=exp(u=j+1∑t​logau​)​

The same gate product multiplies the gradient from St back to an earlier state when gates are treated as fixed: ∂St/∂Sj=∏au. Forgetting old content and attenuating old-state gradients are two consequences of the same recurrence. A channelwise gate assigns different horizons to different state coordinates. It can preserve selected coordinates while discarding others, but cannot retain arbitrary amounts of independent information in a fixed finite-precision state.

Products of many gates can underflow even when their logarithmic sum is representable. Forming ratios gi/gj from two underflowed cumulative products produces 0/0. Instead compute exp(log gi−log gj) over controlled ranges, use stable chunk-local rescaling, and accumulate sensitive reductions in sufficient precision. GLA’s secondary chunking balances these requirements with tensor-core matrix multiplication; log-space bookkeeping itself is not a replacement for the GEMM.

Exercise — Design a decay and check what it means

Choose a fixed gate with half-life 1,024 tokens. What is γ? After 4,096 tokens, what fraction of a write remains? Does this guarantee retrieval of a fact at that distance?

Show worked solution

From γ¹⁰²⁴=1/2, γ=exp(−log2/1024)≈0.9993233275. After 4,096 tokens there have been four half-lives, so γ⁴⁰⁹⁶=1/16=0.0625. This is the multiplier on that write in the linear state. It does not guarantee recall because other writes interfere, the query may not select its key, and later normalization/nonlinear transformations change the readout.

4Fix 2 — the delta rule

Problems defining this stage. Forgetting alone does not correct a value already stored under a similar key. Delta-rule methods target write interference by updating the memory’s prediction error; the algorithmic challenge is parallelizing these dependent matrix updates.

Core idea. DeltaNet reads the value currently associated with a key and writes only the prediction error; Gated DeltaNet additionally decays the state. Compact chunkwise representations of the dependent updates make these selective writes compatible with efficient matrix multiplication.

Decay fixes "never forgets." It does not fix "writes interfere." The delta rule does, and it is the most important idea of the 2024–2026 period.

The problem: to store (k,v)(k, v)(k,v) in an associative memory you would like the state to satisfy S⊤k=vS^\top k = vS⊤k=v. Plain accumulation S←S+kv⊤S \leftarrow S + kv^\top S←S+kv⊤ doesn't achieve this because whatever was already stored under similar keys remains. The classical fix is Widrow–Hoff / delta-rule learning: read the current value, then write the correction.

vold=St−1⊤kt(read)St=St−1+βtkt(vt−vold)⊤(correct)=(I−βtktkt⊤)St−1⏟erase old binding+βtktvt⊤⏟write new binding\begin{aligned}v_{\mathrm{old}}&=S_{t-1}^\top k_t\quad\text{(read)}\\ S_t&=S_{t-1}+\beta_tk_t(v_t-v_{\mathrm{old}})^\top\quad\text{(correct)}\\ &=\underbrace{(I-\beta_tk_tk_t^\top)S_{t-1}}_{\text{erase old binding}}+\underbrace{\beta_tk_tv_t^\top}_{\text{write new binding}}\end{aligned}vold​St​​=St−1⊤​kt​(read)=St−1​+βt​kt​(vt​−vold​)⊤(correct)=erase old binding(I−βt​kt​kt⊤​)St−1​​​+write new bindingβt​kt​vt⊤​​​​

The (I−βkk⊤)(I - \beta kk^\top )(I−βkk⊤) factor is a Householder-like projection — the same family of matrices used in numerical linear algebra to zero out one direction of a vector (see Appendix B). It removes the component of the state aligned with kkk before writing. Now writing a key that was written before replaces rather than superimposes.

Combine with a decay gate and you get Gated DeltaNet, which is the current default recipe:

St=αt(I−βtktkt⊤)St−1+βtktvt⊤αt: global decayβt: strength of binding overwrite\begin{aligned}S_t&=\alpha_t(I-\beta_tk_tk_t^\top)S_{t-1}+\beta_tk_tv_t^\top\\ \alpha_t&:\ \text{global decay}\\ \beta_t&:\ \text{strength of binding overwrite}\end{aligned}St​αt​βt​​=αt​(I−βt​kt​kt⊤​)St−1​+βt​kt​vt⊤​: global decay: strength of binding overwrite​
Two orthogonal mechanisms

α\alpha α is global forgetting — everything fades. β\beta β is targeted overwriting — this key's binding is replaced. Mamba-2 has only α\alpha α; DeltaNet has only β\beta β; Gated DeltaNet has both, and beats both on language modelling, in-context retrieval, length extrapolation and long-context understanding. On memorisation probes, Mamba-2 degrades quickly where Gated DeltaNet holds up — direct evidence that the delta term is what buys recall. 2026 work (Gated DeltaNet-2, KDA) continues down the same road by making the erase and write gates channel-wise and independent.

Why this took four years

The delta rule was computationally awkward: (I−βkk⊤)(I - \beta kk^\top )(I−βkk⊤) is a different matrix at every step, so the chunkwise form's "multiply the state by a fixed decay" trick breaks. The unlock was recognising that a product of Householder matrices has a compact WY representation, which turns the whole chunk's update into a couple of matmuls. The architecture was known; the kernel was the contribution. That is a recurring pattern in this field.

A useful alternative framing, now standard: these recurrences are online learning on a test-time objective. The state is the parameters of an associative-memory model; each token is one optimisation step on ∥S⊤k−v∥2\|S^\top k - v\|^{2}∥S⊤k−v∥2; β\beta β is a learning rate and α\alpha α is weight decay. Test-Time Training layers and Titans make the objective explicit and let you choose the optimiser — momentum, higher-order updates, and so on. Once you see it this way, the design space becomes "which optimiser do you want running inside your forward pass."

Derivation: derive exact overwrite, interference, and the stable learning-rate interval

One online regression update. Let S∈ℝd_k×d_v predict the value as Sᵀk. For loss ℓ(S)=½‖Sᵀk−v‖², differentiating each entry gives ∇Sℓ=k(Sᵀk−v)ᵀ. Gradient descent with step β therefore gives the delta rule S⁺=S+βk(v−Sᵀk)ᵀ.

  1. Read the updated state at the same key: S⁺ᵀk=Sᵀk+β‖k‖²(v−Sᵀk).
  2. Subtract v to get e⁺=(1−β‖k‖²)e, where e=Sᵀk−v.
  3. Hence the current-key error contracts when |1−β‖k‖²|<1, or 0<β‖k‖²<2. Exact one-step overwrite occurs at β=1/‖k‖².
∥k∥=1, β=1  ⟹  (S+)⊤k=v(S+)⊤u−S⊤u=β(k⊤u)(v−S⊤k)\begin{aligned}\|k\|=1,\ \beta=1&\implies(S^+)^\top k=v\\ (S^+)^\top u-S^\top u&=\beta(k^\top u)(v-S^\top k)\end{aligned}∥k∥=1, β=1(S+)⊤u−S⊤u​⟹(S+)⊤k=v=β(k⊤u)(v−S⊤k)​

The second identity quantifies interference: orthogonal keys are unaffected; correlated keys change. The transition A=I−βkkᵀ has eigenvalue 1−β‖k‖² along k and eigenvalue 1 on its orthogonal complement. At unit norm and β=1 it is a projection that erases one direction; at β=2 it is a reflection, which preserves norm rather than contracting. “Householder-like” should not hide these distinctions.

For the gated update S⁺=α(I−βkkᵀ)S+βkvᵀ, interpret the operation as first decay S to αS, then apply a delta update to that decayed state. This yields αS+βk(v−αSᵀk)ᵀ, exactly the stated formula. Applying ordinary weight decay and then computing the error against the old undecayed S would give a different coefficient. Learnable β and key normalization control stability; a stable one-step linear operator alone does not prove stability of the entire nonlinear block.

Exercise — Overwrite is exact only under the right normalization

Take scalar value v=5, key k=(2,0), and state S=(1,3)ᵀ. Compute one delta update for β=1 and for β=1/4. Compare the old and new predictions at k and at the orthogonal key u=(0,1).

Show worked solution

Initially Sᵀk=2 and the residual v−Sᵀk=3. For β=1, S⁺=(1,3)+(2,0)·3=(7,3); the new prediction is 14, so the error has changed from −3 to 9. Its multiplier is 1−β‖k‖²=−3. For β=1/4, S⁺=(1,3)+(1/4)(2,0)·3=(2.5,3), giving prediction 5 exactly. The orthogonal prediction Sᵀu remains 3 in both cases, because kᵀu=0.

Derivation: turn sequential delta updates into a triangular chunk solve

Ungated delta rule inside a chunk. Keep S0 as the incoming state and define the write residual ui=βi(vi−Si−1ᵀki). Then Si=S0+Σj≤ikjujᵀ. Substitute this expression for Si−1 into the definition of ui:

ui=βi[vi−S0⊤ki−∑j<i(ki⊤kj)uj]K∈RC×dk,V,U∈RC×dvB=diag⁡(β1,…,βC)L=strictly_lower⁡(BKK⊤)(I+L)U=B(V−KS0)U=solve_lower⁡(I+L,B(V−KS0))SC=S0+K⊤UO=QS0+[QK⊤⊙Mcausal]U\begin{aligned}u_i&=\beta_i\left[v_i-S_0^\top k_i-\sum_{j<i}(k_i^\top k_j)u_j\right]\\ K&\in\mathbb R^{C\times d_k},\quad V,U\in\mathbb R^{C\times d_v}\\ B&=\operatorname{diag}(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_C)\\ L&=\operatorname{strictly\_lower}(BKK^\top)\\ (I+L)U&=B(V-KS_0)\\ U&=\operatorname{solve\_lower}(I+L,B(V-KS_0))\\ S_C&=S_0+K^\top U\\ O&=QS_0+[QK^\top\odot M_{\mathrm{causal}}]U\end{aligned}ui​KBL(I+L)UUSC​O​=βi​[vi​−S0⊤​ki​−j<i∑​(ki⊤​kj​)uj​]∈RC×dk​,V,U∈RC×dv​=diag(β1​,…,βC​)=strictly_lower(BKK⊤)=B(V−KS0​)=solve_lower(I+L,B(V−KS0​))=S0​+K⊤U=QS0​+[QK⊤⊙Mcausal​]U​

The i-th row of the triangular system is exactly the residual equation above, so this is an algebraic reformulation, not an approximation. I+L has ones on its diagonal and is invertible regardless of the off-diagonal entries. For C=2, u₁=β₁(v₁−S₀ᵀk₁), then u₂=β₂(v₂−S₀ᵀk₂)−β₂(k₂ᵀk₁)u₁. The triangular structure encodes precisely the sequential dependency.

Efficient DeltaNet kernels exploit related compact representations of products of rank-one transitions, often described using WY representations. The important point is that the chunk state update and outputs can be expressed through structured solves and GEMMs without materializing a dense dk×dk transition at every token. Triangular dependencies have not disappeared mathematically; they have been reorganized into operations with better parallel execution. Gate extensions require the corresponding decay factors rather than blindly reusing the ungated equation. Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule.

Exercise — Solve a two-write chunk and compare with recurrence

Let S₀=0, k₁=(1,0), k₂=(1,1), scalar values v₁=2,v₂=3, and β₁=β₂=1/2. Find u₁,u₂ and S₂ using the triangular form, then verify by sequential delta updates.

Show worked solution

The key inner product is k₂ᵀk₁=1. Thus u₁=(1/2)·2=1, and u₂=(1/2)·3−(1/2)·1·1=1. S₂=k₁u₁+k₂u₂=(2,1). Sequentially, S₁=(1,0). It predicts S₁ᵀk₂=1, so its second residual is (1/2)(3−1)=1, adding (1,1) and giving (2,1). Because ‖k₂‖²=2 and β₂=1/2, the second key is overwritten exactly: S₂ᵀk₂=3.

5State-space models are the same thing

Problems defining this stage. SSMs and linear attention arrived with different notation and kernels. The key problem is identifying the overlapping sequence operators so recurrence, structured matrices and matrix-multiplication algorithms can be translated between the two views.

Core idea. Mamba-2’s Structured State-Space Duality expresses the sequence transformation as a structured matrix with both recurrent and attention-like forms. Block decompositions expose matrix multiplications while preserving the recurrence’s compact state.

Mamba and linear attention were developed by different communities with different notation and turn out to be two views of one object. Knowing the dictionary saves you from reading everything twice.

SSM:ht=Aht−1+Bxt,yt=ChtLinear attention:St=αSt−1+ktvt⊤,ot=qt⊤StA⟷α(scalar times I in Mamba-2)B⟷k,C⟷qInput-dependent A,B,C⟷data-dependent gatesChunked scan / SSD⟷chunkwise parallel formSemiseparable matrix⟷Lij=γi−j(causal decay mask)\begin{aligned}\text{SSM:}\quad h_t&=Ah_{t-1}+Bx_t,\quad y_t=Ch_t\\ \text{Linear attention:}\quad S_t&=\alpha S_{t-1}+k_tv_t^\top,\quad o_t=q_t^\top S_t\\ A&\longleftrightarrow\alpha\quad\text{(scalar times }I\text{ in Mamba-2)}\\ B&\longleftrightarrow k,\qquad C\longleftrightarrow q\\ \text{Input-dependent }A,B,C&\longleftrightarrow\text{data-dependent gates}\\ \text{Chunked scan / SSD}&\longleftrightarrow\text{chunkwise parallel form}\\ \text{Semiseparable matrix}&\longleftrightarrow L_{ij}=\gamma^{i-j}\quad\text{(causal decay mask)}\end{aligned}SSM:ht​Linear attention:St​ABInput-dependent A,B,CChunked scan / SSDSemiseparable matrix​=Aht−1​+Bxt​,yt​=Cht​=αSt−1​+kt​vt⊤​,ot​=qt⊤​St​⟷α(scalar times I in Mamba-2)⟷k,C⟷q⟷data-dependent gates⟷chunkwise parallel form⟷Lij​=γi−j(causal decay mask)​

The practical payoff of the duality was algorithmic. SSD replaces Mamba's custom selective-scan kernel with block decompositions of semiseparable matrices, i.e. matmuls — 2–8× faster than the optimised scan while allowing 8× larger state. The lesson generalises: a formulation that reduces to matmul beats a formulation that needs a bespoke scan, even when the scan has better asymptotics, because matmul is what the silicon is for.

The duality also explains why RetNet and TransNormer fit in: they are the special case where the transition is time-invariant, giving the decay mask Li,j=γi−jL_{i,j} = \gamma ^{i-j}Li,j​=γi−j. One remaining architectural difference is inherited from lineage — attention-derived models keep multi-head structure, while Mamba-2's SSM-derived form is naturally multi-value / multi-expand.

Derivation: unroll an SSM and see the attention-shaped matrix

Time-varying linear SSM. Let ht=Atht−1+Btxt and yt=Ctht. Treat input-dependent A,B,C as fixed after they are computed from the sequence. Repeated substitution gives:

ht=At⋯A1h0+∑j=1tAt⋯Aj+1Bjxjyt=CtAt⋯A1h0+∑j≤tMtjxjMtj={CtAt⋯Aj+1Bj,j≤t0,j>t\begin{aligned}h_t&=A_t\cdots A_1h_0+\sum_{j=1}^tA_t\cdots A_{j+1}B_jx_j\\ y_t&=C_tA_t\cdots A_1h_0+\sum_{j\le t}M_{tj}x_j\\ M_{tj}&=\begin{cases}C_tA_t\cdots A_{j+1}B_j,&j\le t\\0,&j>t\end{cases}\end{aligned}ht​yt​Mtj​​=At​⋯A1​h0​+j=1∑t​At​⋯Aj+1​Bj​xj​=Ct​At​⋯A1​h0​+j≤t∑​Mtj​xj​={Ct​At​⋯Aj+1​Bj​,0,​j≤tj>t​​

The empty product for j=t is the identity. When Au=auI, Bj=kj, and Ct=qtᵀ for a scalar-valued input channel, Mtj=(qt⊤kj)∏u=j+1tauM_{tj}=(q_t^\top k_j)\prod_{u=j+1}^ta_uMtj​=(qt⊤​kj​)∏u=j+1t​au​. This is precisely a causal, decay-masked linear-attention matrix. With multiple value channels the same argument applies columnwise to a matrix state.

To see the low-rank structure, cut the sequence at c. For t>c and j≤c, split the transition product at c: Mtj=(CtAt⋯Ac+1)(Ac⋯Aj+1Bj)M_{tj}=(C_tA_t\cdots A_{c+1})(A_c\cdots A_{j+1}B_j)Mtj​=(Ct​At​⋯Ac+1​)(Ac​⋯Aj+1​Bj​). The off-diagonal block factors through the state dimension, so its rank is at most that dimension. This is the semiseparable structure SSD exploits. The duality concerns overlapping operator families; arbitrary nonlinear recurrences, arbitrary transition matrices, and every attention implementation are not interchangeable at equal cost. Input dependence also means the full x↦y mapping is generally nonlinear even though the conditioned sequence operator M is linear.

Use scalar a₁=a₂=a₃=1/2, B=C=1, and h₀=0. Write the 3×3 causal matrix mapping (x₁,x₂,x₃) to (y₁,y₂,y₃). Check it on x=(2,0,4).

M=[100121014121],Mx=[214.5]\begin{aligned}M&=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\\frac12&1&0\\\frac14&\frac12&1\end{bmatrix},\qquad Mx=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\\4.5\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}M​=​121​41​​0121​​001​​,Mx=​214.5​​​
